title: Reproducible chest-wall tenderness: costochondritis
vignette: A 42-year-old woman comes to the emergency department for evaluation of chest pain. She was moving furniture in her summer house 2 days ago when she experienced sharp pain in the left side of the sternum that quickly subsided. Since then, the patient has had episodic pain with deep inspiration or trunk movement. She has no fever or cough. The patient has a history of hypertension. Her father died of myocardial infarction at age 67. She does not use tobacco or illicit drugs. Blood pressure is 146/85 mm Hg in the right arm and 142/80 mm Hg in the left arm, pulse is 86/min, and respirations are 12/min. She has localized tenderness to palpation at the left sternal border. Lungs are clear to auscultation, and cardiac examination reveals normal heart sounds without gallops or murmurs. The abdomen is soft and nontender. There is no peripheral edema. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's symptoms?

clues.text: moving furniture in her summer house 2 days ago
clues.note: Recent repetitive activity/overuse of the chest wall strains the costochondral/costosternal cartilage - the typical trigger for costochondritis.

clues.text: episodic pain with deep inspiration or trunk movement
clues.note: Pain provoked by breathing and movement (positional/pleuritic) is characteristic of a musculoskeletal chest-wall source, not a fixed cardiac lesion.

clues.text: 146/85 mm Hg in the right arm and 142/80 mm Hg in the left arm
clues.note: The tiny inter-arm difference (4-5 mm Hg) is physiologic and NORMAL. It's a trap meant to suggest aortic dissection, but a significant difference is generally >20 mm Hg - so this argues AGAINST dissection.

clues.text: localized tenderness to palpation at the left sternal border
clues.note: Reproducible point tenderness over the costosternal junction is the key confirmatory sign of costochondritis - cardiac, vascular, pulmonary, and GI causes are not tender to palpation.

whatMatters: Pain reproduced by palpation and worsened by movement/inspiration, after moving furniture, with a normal cardiopulmonary exam = costochondritis (costosternal syndrome). Reproducible chest-wall tenderness is the key. Answer C. The near-equal arm blood pressures (a <10-20 mm Hg difference) are normal and don't indicate aortic dissection.
strategy: The single most useful feature is that palpation REPRODUCES the pain and movement/breathing worsen it = musculoskeletal chest-wall pain (costochondritis). Then dismiss the mimics: cardiac/vascular (pericarditis, dissection, unstable angina, pulmonary arterial hypertension) and pulmonary/GI/psychiatric causes don't produce focal reproducible chest-wall tenderness. Don't be baited by the family MI history or the trivial inter-arm BP difference.

eliminations.label: Acute pericarditis - positional/pleuritic, friction rub
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: pericardial inflammation causing pleuritic pain worse supine, better leaning forward, often with a friction rub. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is not reproduced by chest-wall palpation. ✅ Correct if: positional pain + friction rub +/- diffuse ST elevation.

eliminations.label: Aortic dissection - tearing pain + BP asymmetry
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: an intimal tear causing sudden tearing pain radiating to the back, often with a large (>20 mm Hg) inter-arm BP difference. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: here the arm pressures are essentially equal (4-5 mm Hg) and the pain is positional/reproducible. ✅ Correct if: tearing pain with significant pulse/BP asymmetry and a widened mediastinum.

eliminations.label: Esophageal spasm - swallow/meal-related
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: diffuse esophageal spasm causing retrosternal pain that can mimic angina. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it relates to swallowing/meals, not palpation or trunk movement. ✅ Correct if: dysphagia or meal-triggered chest pain.

eliminations.label: Gastroesophageal reflux disease - burning, postprandial
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: acid reflux causing burning retrosternal pain, worse postprandial/nocturnal. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is not tender to palpation and isn't movement-provoked. ✅ Correct if: heartburn relieved by antacids.

eliminations.label: Panic disorder - anxiety, diagnosis of exclusion
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: episodic chest pain with intense anxiety, palpitations, and dyspnea. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it lacks chest-wall tenderness and is a diagnosis of exclusion. ✅ Correct if: recurrent anxiety attacks without organic findings.

eliminations.label: Pneumonia - infectious
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: lung infection with fever, productive cough, and focal crackles. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: no fever, cough, or crackles here. ✅ Correct if: febrile respiratory illness with consolidation.

eliminations.label: Pulmonary arterial hypertension - exertional dyspnea
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: elevated pulmonary pressures with exertional dyspnea, loud P2, and right-heart signs. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it doesn't cause focal reproducible chest-wall pain. ✅ Correct if: progressive dyspnea with RV strain.

eliminations.label: Pulmonary embolism - pleuritic + dyspnea/hypoxia
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: pleuritic chest pain with dyspnea, tachycardia, and hypoxia in an at-risk patient. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: no dyspnea/hypoxia/risk factors, and PE isn't tender to palpation. ✅ Correct if: sudden dyspnea/hypoxia with DVT risk.

eliminations.label: Unstable angina - exertional pressure
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: crescendo exertional chest pressure radiating to arm/jaw, relieved by rest/nitrates. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: reproducible local tenderness argues against a cardiac cause. ✅ Correct if: exertional chest pressure with ischemic features.

reasoning: Pain worse with movement/inspiration and REPRODUCED by palpation, with a normal cardiopulmonary exam
Near-equal arm blood pressures exclude aortic dissection (and no ischemic features)
mechanism: Costochondritis (costosternal syndrome/anterior chest wall syndrome) is inflammation of the costochondral or costosternal cartilage, typically following repetitive activity or overuse of the chest wall. It produces localized anterior chest pain that is REPRODUCIBLE with palpation and worsened by movement, deep inspiration, or positional change, without warmth, swelling, or systemic signs. Because it is a benign musculoskeletal process, the cardiopulmonary examination is normal, and the small (<10 mm Hg) physiologic inter-arm blood-pressure difference here is normal and does not suggest aortic dissection. Diagnosis is clinical after excluding cardiac, vascular, pulmonary, esophageal, and anxiety-related causes - none of which produce focal reproducible chest-wall tenderness.

difficulty.label: 📚 Pure knowledge gap
difficulty.message: First Aid MSK/CV > costochondritis (reproducible chest-wall tenderness, benign, after overuse); the chest-pain differential table.

difficulty.label: 🧭 Understanding the question
difficulty.message: Weight 'reproducible with palpation' as the decisive clue and treat the family MI history and trivial BP difference as red herrings.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocabulary
difficulty.message: Unsure on costochondral/costosternal, pleuritic, inter-arm BP difference, or gallops/murmurs? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🧲 Pulled by a distractor
difficulty.message: Aortic dissection is the intended trap (BP in both arms is listed), but the difference is normal; angina/pericarditis/PE don't cause focal chest-wall tenderness.

difficulty.label: ✍️ Something else
difficulty.message: Bank: chest pain REPRODUCED by palpation + worse with movement/breathing + normal exam = costochondritis; inter-arm BP difference must be >~20 mm Hg to suggest dissection.

keywords.front: Chest pain reproduced by palpation + worse with movement/breathing

keywords.back: <10-20 mm Hg is normal (argues against dissection)

keywords.front: Significant inter-arm BP difference + tearing pain to back

keywords.back: Worse supine, better leaning forward; friction rub
Repetitive activity / overuse of the chest wall
Focal chest-wall tenderness -> musculoskeletal, not cardiac

memoryHook: If your finger can find the pain, the heart is probably fine - press the sternum, reproduce it: costochondritis.
